articles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Findings in Simple Elbow Dislocations: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Sachinis NP, Bhardwaj V, Scaglia M, Gerace F, Christiane Messina J, Randelli PS, et al.
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of soft tissue injuries (medial and lateral collateral ligament damage) and osteochondral injuries on MRI following simple elbow dislocation
articles.take_home: MRI scans after simple elbow dislocations commonly show damage to the ligaments that stabilise the elbow, but routine MRI scanning is not recommended for every patient. MRI may be helpful when doctors are unsure if the elbow is stable after reduction or when additional information might change treatment decisions.

articles.title: Hyperlipidemia Is Associated With an Increased Risk of Secondary Procedures in Patients Undergoing Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair.
articles.authors: Prabhavalkar ON, Morriss NJ, Malin M, Jain S, Dussik CM, Phan A, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using federated database
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
articles.outcomes: Repeat rotator cuff repair and shoulder replacement at 6 months, 1, 3, and 5 years
articles.take_home: Patients with high cholesterol had slightly higher rates of needing further shoulder surgery after rotator cuff repair compared to those without high cholesterol. Taking statins did not reduce the need for further surgery and was linked to higher reoperation rates in patients with low cholesterol.

articles.title: Comparison of Clinical Outcome and Return to Work Following Exactech Equinoxe Reverse Total Shoulder Arthroplasty: Pectoralis Major Tendon Transfer versus Subscapularis Repair.
articles.authors: Baek CH, Lim C, Kim JG, Kim BT, Kim SJ
articles.population: Patients undergoing reverse total shoulder arthroplasty for rotator cuff tear arthropathy
articles.sample_size: 69 patients (42 subscapularis repair, 27 pectoralis major transfer)
articles.outcomes: Activities of Daily Living involving Internal Rotation score, return to work rate, internal rotation range of motion and strength, tendon retear rates on imaging
articles.take_home: Pectoralis major tendon transfer produced better internal rotation function and was more likely to allow return to heavy work compared with subscapularis repair. Pectoralis major transfer had no retears while subscapularis repair failed in 31% of patients, suggesting it may be a better option when subscapularis repair is not possible.

articles.title: Data-Driven Preoperative Hemoglobin Strata Predict Blood Transfusion and Surgical Complication Risk Following Total Shoulder Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Clements J, Shen V, Tan D, Ranson R, Shah A, Zimmer Z
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using large database
articles.population: Patients undergoing total shoulder arthroplasty with preoperative hemoglobin values recorded
articles.outcomes: 90-day blood transfusion, major complications, wound infection, dehiscence, 2-year revision surgery, periprosthetic joint infection, and mechanical loosening
articles.take_home: Lower preoperative hemoglobin levels are associated with increased risk of blood transfusion, infection, and other complications after shoulder replacement surgery. The study identified different hemoglobin thresholds for men and women that help predict these risks.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes and Predictors of Dissatisfaction Following Revision Surgery After Distal Clavicle Excision.
articles.authors: Fiandeiro M, Patil R, Su F, Singh A, Lee S, Khoury E, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent revision surgery after distal clavicle excision between 2005 and 2024
articles.sample_size: 46 shoulders (28 males, 18 females), mean age 48.3 years
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS), shoulder function (ASES and SANE scores), patient satisfaction, subjective instability, complications and reoperations at minimum 24 months follow-up
articles.take_home: Revision surgery after failed distal clavicle excision improved pain and function for most patients, but a third remained dissatisfied and reported feeling the shoulder was still unstable. Patients who felt their shoulder was unstable were much more likely to be unhappy with their surgery results.

articles.title: Length of stay, discharge disposition, and 90-day emergency department visits and readmissions following primary shoulder arthroplasty in octogenarians vs septuagenarians.
articles.authors: Lorentz S, Hurley ET, Levin JM, Cullen M, Crook BS, Karavan MP, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 70-89 years undergoing primary shoulder arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Hospital length of stay, discharge location, 90-day emergency department visits and readmissions
articles.take_home: Patients in their 80s who have shoulder replacement surgery stay in hospital about half a day longer and are more likely to need rehabilitation facility care after discharge compared to those in their 70s, but they have similar rates of emergency department visits and readmissions within 90 days.

articles.title: Effects of grip contraction with different finger recruitment and different wrist positions on dynamic medial elbow joint stability.
articles.authors: Sato R, Ishigaki T, Okochi T, Sakamoto K, Kato Y, Hirabayashi R, et al.
articles.outcomes: Medial elbow joint space measured by ultrasound during grip contraction with different finger recruitment and wrist positions
articles.take_home: Using your index finger (second digit) when gripping is particularly important for stabilising the inside of the elbow joint. Gripping with your wrist bent forward (palmar flexion) provides less stability to the inner elbow than gripping with your wrist in a neutral position.

articles.title: Predictors of External Rotation Recovery following Reverse Shoulder Arthroplasty in Patients with Preoperative Lag Signs.
articles.authors: Boubekri AM, Zmistowski B, Devana SK, Keener JD
articles.population: Patients with preoperative external rotation lag signs undergoing reverse shoulder arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 55 primary reverse shoulder arthroplasty patients with minimum 2-year follow-up
articles.outcomes: External rotation recovery in adduction and abduction plane, forward elevation, functional external rotation achievement, ASES scores
articles.take_home: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty reliably improves external rotation in patients with lag signs, but recovery depends mainly on how much external rotation and lag the patient had before surgery rather than on implant positioning. Patients with better preoperative external rotation and smaller lag signs are more likely to achieve good functional results from surgery alone.

articles.title: Risk factors and management of atraumatic distal clavicular osteolysis: A scoping review.
articles.authors: Wilkinson M, Groch N, Freestone CA, Clements A, Obst S
articles.population: Patients with atraumatic distal clavicular osteolysis
articles.outcomes: Risk factors for ADCO, clinical and radiographic features, indications for surgery, recovery rates with conservative and surgical management
articles.take_home: Bench pressing and weight training are common risk factors for this shoulder condition. Most patients improve with non-surgical treatment, but about 16% need surgery, which generally works well.
